/-!
# Erdős Problem 653

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/653](https://www.erdosproblems.com/653)
-/

open Finset EuclideanGeometry Filter

namespace Erdos653

/-- Let $x_1,\ldots,x_n\in \mathbb{R}^2$ and let $R(x_i)=\#\{ \lvert x_j-x_i\rvert : j\neq i\}$,
where the points are ordered such that
$$R(x_1)\leq \cdots \leq R(x_n).$$
Let $g(n)$ be the maximum number of distinct values the $R(x_i)$ can take. Is it true that
$g(n) \geq (1-o(1))n$? -/
@[category research open, AMS 5 52]
theorem erdos_653 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ o : ℕ → ℝ, o =o[atTop] (1 : ℕ → ℝ) ∧
    ∀ᶠ n in atTop, (1 - o n) * n ≤ maximalDistinctDistancesFrom n := by
  sorry

end Erdos653

reformulations.difference: The source's maximum and asymptotic lower bound are represented using a natural-number supremum and an existential real error sequence satisfying an eventual inequality.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For each n, the attainable numbers of distinct R-values form a nonempty set of naturals bounded by n. Thus the natural supremum is an attained maximum; its default for unbounded sets is unreachable. The condition o =o[atTop] 1 means o(n)→0. Since g(n)≤n, the theorem's right-hand side is equivalent to g(n)/n→1: eventually 1−o(n)≤g(n)/n≤1, and conversely one can choose o(n)=1−g(n)/n. Both the lower-bound/existence-of-configuration equivalence and this asymptotic equivalence were proved in the scratch file.
